approach: Ship the standalone as a host shell (src/gramtrans/standalone/) that reproduces what FlexTools hands the module - an open source project, a report sink, modifyAllowed - and calls the unchanged MainFunction. Freeze it with one PyInstaller spec producing an Inno Setup installer plus a best-effort onefile, built in a throwaway venv from a hash-pinned build-only lock so pyproject floors stay untouched. Non-regression is enforced by five enumerated shared-code exceptions, all additive with FlexTools-preserving defaults, plus a CI gate that runs from the first commit.

decisions.decision: The Move confirmation gate is a host-supplied duck-typed object threaded through MainFunction -> SelectionWizard -> _PageFinish as one keyword-only parameter defaulting to AlwaysSatisfiedGate.
decisions.why: FR-017 needs the gate reachable from the wizard but owned by the host; a permissive default makes the FlexTools path byte-identical (SC-013) with no new dialog or step.
decisions.rejected: Embedding the gate in the wizard (gives every FlexTools user a redundant blocking dialog), and having the shell construct SelectionWizard directly (forks the QApplication setup, fatal-exception funnel and FR-013 target cleanup that MainFunction owns).

decisions.decision: {"decision": "The shell does no registry access of its own; it calls flexicon.FLExInitialize() and reads flexicon.code.FLExGlobals module attributes post-init.", "why": "InitialiseFWGlobals already probes HKCU/HKLM SOFTWARE\SIL\FieldWorks\9, validates FieldWorks.exe, appends only FWCodeDir to sys.path and reads the version from FieldWorks itself - which is the whole of FR-001/031/032/033/044. The package-level re-exports (flexicon.FWProjectsDir) bind before init and stay None, so they must never be read.", "rejected": "An own winreg probe in the shell - duplicates the logic and can report a code dir different from the one whose assemblies were actually loaded."}

Keep the flat site.addsitedir import convention and absorb it in packaging: generate hiddenimports by globbing Lib/**/*.py and declaring every module under BOTH its flat top-level name and its gramtrans.Lib.* package name.
decisions.why: FR-018 forbids the import refactor and 31 files carry if __package__ dual-mode guards; PyInstaller FrozenImporter resolves top-level names from the archive directly, so the guards keep taking their flat branch. Generation rather than a hand-list means a new helper needs no build-file edit.
decisions.rejected: Shipping Lib/ as --add-data and relying on addsitedir at runtime (ships source, defers every import error to runtime), and refactoring the imports (forbidden outright by FR-018).

decisions.decision: Constitution reconciliation takes Question 1 Option C (narrow amendment) and Send/Receive takes the owner custom answer: state the recovery path, do not detect or restrict.
decisions.why: Option C sanctions exactly one standalone Windows host artifact and the components it bundles, and records the Principle III undo exception against that artifact alone, so both general constraints keep their force. The S/R procedure (S/R first; on a bad run delete the local project and receive again) is equally true under FlexTools, so detection machinery in the standalone alone would imply otherwise and add a mis-detection failure mode for nothing.
decisions.rejected: Options A/B/D for governance; and detect-and-refuse or detect-and-warn for Send/Receive targets.

decisions.decision: Exact pins live only in build/requirements.lock (hash-pinned, consumed by a throwaway venv); pyproject.toml keeps its version floors.
decisions.why: FR-019/FR-041 keep FlexTools installs unconstrained by this feature, and FR-042 rules out resolving anything from the build machine. Hashes make SC-008 checkable rather than hoped-for.
decisions.rejected: Pinning in pyproject.toml (constrains every FlexTools install), and substituting a stand-in flextoolslib shim for the six FTM_* names (a fork of host metadata that can drift; rejected by the spec assumptions).

decisions.decision: SC-011 is enforced as a non-regression check against a pinned baseline of 27 known failures, not as a bare pytest step
decisions.why: 27 tests under features 026/029 already fail on a clean main. A gate step that is red from the feature's first commit enforces nothing and gets ignored, which is the exact failure FR-021 (continuously during development) exists to prevent. The wrapper fails on any NEW failure and on any baseline entry that starts passing, so the list can only shrink and only deliberately.
decisions.rejected: A bare `pytest -m "not integration"` step as tasks.md literally specified, or fixing the 27 (another feature's work)

decisions.decision: FR-031 (FieldWorks missing) is detected around `import flexicon`, not around FLExInitialize()
decisions.why: Measured on flexicon 4.3.1: FLExInit.py calls InitialiseFWGlobals() at module scope and it raises when the registry key is absent, with nothing guarding it -- so the import itself fails and FLExInitialize() is never reached. Research R1 had this backwards.
decisions.rejected: The contract's original ordering, which put the FieldWorks-missing check on FLExInitialize()

decisions.decision: projects_root is threaded MainFunction -> _run_gui -> SelectionWizard -> initialize_run, widening exception rows 1 and 2
decisions.why: Exception 4 made RunContextStub.projects_root injectable, but the shell never calls initialize_run -- SelectionWizard.__init__ does. The value has to travel the same path as confirmation_gate. Same files, same additive keyword-only defaulted shape.
decisions.rejected: A module-level default in gt_api set by the shell -- hidden global state shared by both hosts

decisions.decision: FR-028/FR-029 are rendered as plain language at the raise site in Lib/api.py rather than at a new render site
decisions.why: The wizard already shows str(e) for SameProjectError and TargetUnavailable, so the smallest change that stops raw developer text reaching a user is to write the exception text in plain language. Not imported from gramtrans.standalone.errors, because FR-016 forbids shared code depending on the shell.
decisions.rejected: Intercepting the exceptions in the shell, which would mean re-implementing the wizard's error dialogs

decisions.why: PyQt6 6.11.0 raises ImportError: DLL load failed while importing QtCore on this platform -- measured unfrozen in a clean venv, with both the matched 6.11.0 and the 6.11.1 that PyQt6's own too-loose pin resolves to. 6.7.1 is what every test and every live parity run used, and a build lock exists to ship the versions that were validated. pyproject.toml keeps its >=6.4 floor: the ceiling constrains the artifact, not FlexTools installs.
decisions.rejected: Letting the lock float to the newest PyQt6, which produces an artifact whose UI cannot start

decisions.decision: HostSession.release() does not clear the fwglobals initialised flag
decisions.why: FLExCleanup() ends the SLDR/ICU session, but the FieldWorks globals were read from the registry at import and remain true. Clearing the flag made a later read raise a startup-ordering error that was simply false.
decisions.rejected: Treating the flag as session-scoped, which broke every test that used a HostSession and then read fwglobals

decisions.decision: SC-005 is verified against the .fwdata.lock file plus a subprocess re-open, not by re-opening write-enabled in-process
decisions.why: Measured: LCM keeps per-process state that fails a second write-open of an already-used project even after every handle is closed and the lock file is gone. The in-process check reports leaks that are not there.
decisions.rejected: Re-opening the source with writeEnabled=True in the test process

plan.summary: Plan, research, data model and three contracts written; both open questions resolved and encoded back into spec.md; non-regression pinned to five enumerated shared-code exceptions.
plan.key_finding: flexicon already implements FieldWorks discovery, version validation and the sys.path addition (FR-001/031/032/044) in InitialiseFWGlobals - but its package-level re-exports (flexicon.FWProjectsDir) bind before FLExInitialize() and stay None, so the shell and self-check must read flexicon.code.FLExGlobals module attributes post-init or report a false failure on a healthy machine.

tasks.summary: Fifty-six tasks in seven phases. Phase 2 now also contains T012, which converts the research-R1 flexicon-globals trap from a review habit into a CI failure: a sole accessor module, a None-means-runtime-failed mapping so the bug cannot present as a false "FieldWorks not installed", and an AST ban wired into the regression gate so it guards Phases 3-6 as they are written. Every FR-001..FR-054 maps to at least one task.

concerns.note: The regression workflow has never executed on GitHub. The branch 034-standalone-windows-app is unpushed and this repository had no Actions history before this feature. Every step was verified locally, but SC-012 (no commit merges with a red gate) cannot be called measured until the branch is pushed and the workflow goes green.

Inno Setup (ISCC.exe) is not installed on this machine, so GramTrans-Setup-<version>.exe -- the SUPPORTED artifact -- has never been produced. The onedir program it wraps is fully smoke-tested; the wrapper is not. A release build must run where ISCC.exe is available.

SC-001 (download to completed preview in under 10 minutes, unassisted) and SC-007 (90% of support cases resolved without a round-trip) are user-observation criteria and are recorded as NOT MEASURED rather than assumed green. Both need a real person who has not seen the application before.

27 tests under features 026 (texts/wordforms) and 029 (sense pictures) plus one wizard POS-closure test fail on a clean main and are baselined, not fixed. Out of scope for 034, but the baseline is a standing debt: it should shrink, and .github/known-failures.txt fails the build if any entry starts passing so it cannot rot silently.

PyQt6 is pinned <6.8 in the build lock because 6.11 does not load on this platform at all. That was measured on ONE machine (Windows 11 26200, Python 3.12.7). If the ceiling turns out to be machine-specific rather than a genuine Qt 6.11 platform requirement, the pin is more conservative than it needs to be -- worth re-testing on a second machine before it calcifies.
